claims.text: A ZrB2 cermet containing 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr binder can be consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1500 °C.
The 1500 °C cermet will have superior density, mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and wear resistance compared with pure ZrB2 and cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The starting ceramic powder is greater than 99.8% pure ZrB2 with a particle size of 1–5 μm.
The AlFeNiCoCr binder is formed from equimolar quantities of Al, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr.
The proposed SPS schedule is 1500 °C under vacuum and 50 MPa, using an approximately 200 °C/min heating rate and a 5-minute hold.
At 1500 °C, the AlFeNiCoCr binder becomes liquid and has sufficient fluidity to fill pores uniformly.
Binder flow at 1500 °C promotes strong interdendritic bonding between ZrB2 grains.
Sintering at 1500 °C produces approximately 97.71% relative density and a compact, coherent microstructure.
Enhanced pore filling and grain bonding improve densification and mechanical integrity.
The dense microstructure reduces pathways for molten-aluminum penetration.
The dense microstructure suppresses detachment of ZrB2 grains.
Reduced penetration and grain detachment increase hardness, fracture toughness, oxidation resistance, and molten-aluminum corrosion resistance while reducing abrasive wear.
Sintering at 1600 °C causes binder overflow, introduces porosity, and degrades performance.
Among the compared sintering temperatures, the 1500 °C specimen will have the highest relative density.
The 1500 °C specimen will have greater fracture toughness than the approximately 4.5 MPa·m^1/2 value attributed to pure ZrB2.
Pure ZrB2 has a known fracture toughness of approximately 4.5 MPa·m^1/2.
The 1500 °C specimen will exhibit the lowest molten-aluminum corrosion rate, minimal wear volume, and more stable friction behavior.
The claimed corrosion performance applies to exposure in molten aluminum at 700 °C for no more than 12 days.
Long-term stability beyond the proposed test duration has not been established.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts superiority over pure ZrB2, but the experiment includes only four ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr temperature groups and no concurrently prepared pure-ZrB2 control, so that comparison cannot be decisively tested.
Improved oxidation resistance is claimed, but the experiment specifies no oxidation exposure, mass-change measurement, oxide-scale characterization, or oxidation-based falsification criterion.
